<a id="why"></a>

## Why

pij's earlier requirement register stays archived where it was written and is not copied here. Its open rows were checked one by one against today's code: rows the code already meets (checked against file and test), and rows about the retired TypeScript daemon generation, were dropped. The rows still true are written here fresh, so pij's public repo holds one live list of what is left to build. The triage record is docs/plans/192-prd-register-move/assets/evidence/triage.md.

<a id="actors"></a>

## Actors

| id | name | need |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a-operator | operator | Trust what the fleet reports, and never have a message typed over their own typing. |
| a-prime | prime | A true picture of which seats are alive, where, and on which daemon. |
| a-seat | any seat | Send and receive whole messages and recover from its own startup failures. |

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

| id | goal |
| --- | --- |
| g-1 | Every message has a known sender, and the sender hears how it ended. |
| g-2 | Seats and daemons are easy to tell apart, and each seat talks to the daemon that made it. |
| g-3 | Every pij verb works or is retired on purpose. |

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non goals

| id | text |
| --- | --- |
| n-1 | The community directory and its verbs (PRD 001). |
| n-2 | The earlier register's history, its done rows and its wording. |
| n-3 | Work inside other projects that read pij's HTTP API; pij's side (/v1/seats, /v1/events) exists. |

| req-01 | Claude socket hold and deny receipts are proven live | When a Claude seat's operator holds or denies a socket message, the sender's receipt says held or denied, shown against a real Claude session and not only a stand-in socket. | any seat | should | [ ] planned | A live run against the current Claude build ends in a held receipt when the operator has not yet approved, and in a refused receipt when the operator denies. | triage of the earlier register, 2026-11-04 | — | crates/transport/src/uds.rs:51-54 marks the hold and deny decoder as unproven on the daemon's connection shape; its tests (uds.rs:1459-1593) use a stand-in socket. Spawns already accept inbound by default (crates/cli/src/main.rs:2858-2864). |
| req-02 | Revive can preview what it would do | `pij-rs revive` can show the launch it would make without changing any seat row or starting anything. | any seat | should | [ ] planned | A revive preview prints the planned launch and leaves the seat row and tmux unchanged. | triage of the earlier register, 2026-11-04 | — | `pij-rs revive --help` lists no preview option. Recycled-pid checks exist (docs/how/pij-rs-api.md:1018-1038), and a live seat that lost its binding re-binds with `pij-rs adopt &lt;pane&gt;`. |
| req-03 | Spawn can hand a seat its first task | `pij-rs spawn` can carry a first task that the new seat receives once, after it has bound, so it starts work without a separate send. | any seat | should | [ ] planned | A spawn given a task yields a seat whose first turn is that task, delivered exactly once. | triage of the earlier register, 2026-11-04 | — | crates/cli/src/main.rs:274-323 offers `--cwd` and no task field. |
| req-04 | Work trees come with their own cleanup | Making a stream's work tree also scaffolds its numbered plan folder and can bind the seat to it, and a matching teardown deletes the tree and branch along with any build output the seat left, refusing while uncommitted or unpushed work remains. | any seat | should | [ ] planned | Create then remove leaves no tree, branch or build directory behind; removing a tree with uncommitted changes refuses and loses nothing. | triage of the earlier register, 2026-11-04 | — | `pij-rs stream create` makes the worktree and branch (crates/daemon/src/orchestration/repo.rs:68-93); nothing under crates/daemon/src/orchestration/ removes a worktree or scaffolds a plan. |
| req-05 | A seat talks to the daemon that spawned it | A seat spawned by a non-default daemon, such as a private test daemon, is given that daemon's address and state directory, so its replies go back there and never to the main daemon. | any seat | should | [ ] planned | A seat spawned by a private daemon replies to that daemon, and a reused pane id cannot cause a second adopt on the main daemon. | triage of the earlier register, 2026-11-04 | — | crates/harnesses/src/spawn.rs:142-146 passes PIJ_SESSION_ID and PIJ_SPAWN_ID to the child, not PIJ_RS_ADDR or PIJ_RS_STATE_DIR. |
| req-06 | Each unported verb is ported or retired on purpose | Every verb the `pij` shim still answers with E-RS-UNPORTED (peer transcript tail, models, tree, watch and the rest) is either ported or removed from the shim's list, and the word tail names one thing. | any seat | should | [ ] planned | `pij --help` lists no E-RS-UNPORTED verb, and reading a peer's transcript has its own verb name. | triage of the earlier register, 2026-11-04 | — | Unported verbs refuse by name today (.omp/extensions/pij/cli.ts:57); peer transcript tail is one of them (.omp/extensions/pij/core/generation-routing.ts:303) while `pij-rs tail` follows daemon events (crates/cli/src/main.rs:1702-1727). |
| req-07 | Several daemons are easy to tell apart | When a seat or message can't be found, pij says whether it belongs to another running daemon and lists the daemons that are up; a message queued but undeliverable says so. | any seat | should | [ ] planned | With two daemons running, looking up a seat that lives on the other one names that daemon, and one command lists both. | triage of the earlier register, 2026-11-04 | — | `pij generation` is only a routing check (.omp/extensions/pij/cli.ts:71-75); the daemon's routes (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:596-660) include no daemon listing. |
| req-08 | Typecheck covers test files | `just typecheck` checks test files as well, so a test that would not compile cannot pass unnoticed. | any seat | should | [ ] planned | A deliberately ill-typed test file makes `just typecheck` fail. | triage of the earlier register, 2026-11-04 | — | tsconfig.json:19 excludes **/*.test.ts. |
| req-09 | Every message has a known sender | A message in a seat's inbox comes from a registered seat or is plainly marked unverified, and the recipient can always reply to whoever sent it. | any seat | must | [ ] planned | A send whose sender is not a registered seat is refused or arrives marked unverified, and a reply to any delivered message reaches its sender. | triage of the earlier register, 2026-11-04 | — | `pij send` through the shim derives the sender (crates/daemon/src/http/shim.rs:611-627), but /v1/send takes the body's `from` and refuses only pij-bg (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1689-1700), and delivery routes that sender without a registry lookup (crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:991-1025). |
| req-10 | Wire changes ship with a restart and tolerate one version back | A change to the daemon's wire version ships with a daemon restart and a notice to the fleet in the same step, and clients accept the previous version. | any seat | should | [ ] planned | A client built for version N reads a version N-1 envelope, and the restart and fleet notice go out together. | triage of the earlier register, 2026-11-04 | — | The extension accepts only envelope v2 (.omp/extensions/pij/core/daemon-wire.ts:263-265), and `just bounce-rs` (justfile:569-583) sends no fleet notice. |
| req-11 | Anyone can look at a seat's queue without touching it | A read-only view lists the messages waiting for any seat, why each waits and when it is next tried, without claiming or changing them. | any seat | should | [ ] planned | The view shows a waiting message with its reason and next try, and the message is still delivered afterwards. | triage of the earlier register, 2026-11-04 | — | crates/store/src/queue.rs:792-799 has an internal peek; no route in crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:596-660 exposes a seat's queue. |
| req-12 | A sender hears when a queued message lands | When a send is queued instead of delivered, the sender gets one later notice in its own inbox or card when the message is delivered or given up. | any seat | should | [ ] planned | A sender whose message was queued gets exactly one notice when it is delivered, and one when it is given up. | triage of the earlier register, 2026-11-04 | — | Outcomes are published as `delivery.outcome` events keyed to the recipient (crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:32-34, 854); nothing reaches the sender.
